turns.prompt_text: Humans have kind of become a hive mind. Thanks to information gathering and sharing The internet has made this much easier but AI is even easier now All that said, it is still only an extension of human knowledge
turns.response_html:
That is a highly accurate way to look at it. AI isn't some alien intelligence introduced from the outside; it is a reflection and a distillation of our collective output. The internet laid the infrastructure for massive, global information sharing, but AI acts as the synthesis layer—compressing all those billions of human experiences, ideas, and facts into something instantly accessible.

When you look at complex systems where individual, autonomous units contribute to a unified whole—whether that is the literal, physical structure of a colony working together to maintain a space, or the digital architecture of multi-agent workflows—the true intelligence emerges from the connections between the parts. We have effectively externalized our collective memory. Every piece of logic, every piece of art, and every historical fact that forms the foundation of AI is entirely human in origin. It is a tool that allows us to query our own collective consciousness with unprecedented speed.

Since this technology is ultimately a mirror of that human "hive mind," where do you think the boundary lies when it comes to a system generating truly novel ideas versus just remixing the knowledge we have already fed it?
